theVillage.finalCtaBody: Fresh food, all day, in the heart of Hargeisa's Sha'ab Area.
theVillage.whatsappGreeting: Hello The Village Hargeisa 👋 I found you on Go Hargeisa and would like to ask about the menu and a table.
theVillage.heroPhotoAlt: The Village Hargeisa open-air terrace at golden hour — tiled tables under cream parasols beside a planted bed, with a warm sunset sky.
theVillage.storyIntro: Hand-worked walls, woven lantern light and an open terrace under the Hargeisa sky. A look around before you visit.
theVillage.story_diningRoom_body: A long covered terrace runs beneath a reed-and-timber ceiling, lined with cushioned benches and hand-inlaid tables. Sculpted arches and woven pendant lights give the room its calm, unhurried character.
theVillage.photoAlt_diningRoom: The Village Hargeisa covered dining terrace — cushioned benches along a sculpted arched wall, inlaid wooden tables and iron chairs beneath a reed ceiling and a large woven pendant lamp.
theVillage.story_outdoor_body: Out on the open terrace, tables sit in the shade of wide parasols beside a small stone water feature and a young tree. It's the seat to take on a bright afternoon or an easy weekend.
theVillage.photoAlt_outdoor: The Village Hargeisa outdoor terrace by day — iron bistro tables shaded by cream parasols, a small stone water feature and a young tree against a blue sky.
theVillage.story_evening_body: After dark, a run of woven straw pendants lights the room in low amber. Warm reflections cross the floor, and the arched niches along the wall pick up the glow.
theVillage.photoAlt_evening: The Village Hargeisa dining hall at night — a row of woven straw pendant lamps glowing amber over iron chairs and tables, with lit arched wall niches.
theVillage.story_lamplight_body: Straw pendants hang low from a reed-and-beam ceiling, keeping the light soft and warm across the room.
theVillage.photoAlt_lamplight: The Village Hargeisa ceiling — a timber-beamed reed ceiling with a large woven straw pendant lamp glowing warm.
theVillage.story_featureWall_body: A relief wall of rounded niches, each cradling a smooth stone — the kind of detail you only notice once you've sat down.
theVillage.photoAlt_featureWall: The Village Hargeisa interior feature wall — hand-sculpted adobe with rounded recesses, each holding a smooth stone, beneath woven pendant lamps and a reed ceiling.
theVillage.story_archMirror_body: A gilded sunburst mirror centred in a white plaster arch, an iron lantern warm beside it — the calm, symmetrical detailing that carries through the room.
theVillage.photoAlt_archMirror: The Village Hargeisa interior — a gold sunburst mirror centred in a white plastered arch, with a lit iron wall lantern to the right, below a timber-beamed reed ceiling.
theVillage.story_pendant_body: Each pendant is a hand-woven basket of cane and rattan, glowing from within against the dark ceiling.
theVillage.photoAlt_pendant: A hand-woven cane-and-rattan pendant lamp at The Village Hargeisa, lit from within against a dark reed-panelled ceiling.
theVillage.story_arrival_body: The mark glows warm off the wall at the entrance, above a low bed of flowers — the first thing you see, and the last.
theVillage.photoAlt_arrival: The Village Hargeisa entrance at night — the backlit restaurant emblem glowing warm on a dark textured wall above a lit flower bed.

diasporaWeek.aboutBody1: Somaliland Diaspora Week brings sons and daughters of the nation home to Hargeisa — from Minneapolis to London, Nairobi to Dubai — for five days of reconnection, dialogue and celebration. It is a moment to stand together, share ideas and reaffirm a shared identity.
diasporaWeek.aboutBody2: This year's theme, "Internal Cohesion is the Key to Recognition," reflects a simple truth: unity at home is the foundation everything else is built on. Through cultural festivals, investment forums, youth panels and community town halls, Diaspora Week 2026 is about building that foundation together.

privacy.sharingText: We use Supabase to host our database, authentication, and file storage — your account and content data resides with them as our data processor, under their own security safeguards. privacy.retentionText: We keep your account data for as long as your account is active. You can permanently delete your account and all associated data (reviews, favorites, saved trips) at any time from Account Settings in your dashboard — no need to contact us. privacy.mobileText: The Go Hargeisa app requests only the permissions it needs to function: internet access, network-status detection (to show an offline screen when needed), notification delivery (only if you enable it), and vibration (for interface feedback). travelGuide.title: Hargeisa Travel Guide
travelGuide.subtitle: Practical information to help you plan a smooth trip
travelGuide.infoSubtitle: From visas to safety tips, here's what to expect.
travelGuide.visaBody: Most nationalities can obtain a Somaliland visa on arrival at Egal International Airport (HGA), or in advance from a Somaliland representative office abroad. Bring two passport photos and pay the fee in USD.
travelGuide.airportBody: Egal International Airport (HGA) sits about 5 km from the city center. Taxis and hotel shuttles are available outside arrivals; agree on a fare before departing.
travelGuide.transportBody: Shared and private taxis are the main way to get around the city. Ride-hailing apps are limited, so hotels can arrange trusted drivers for day trips and airport transfers.
travelGuide.currencyBody: The Somaliland shilling (SLSH) is the local currency, though US dollars are widely accepted for hotels, larger purchases and taxis. Mobile money (Zaad, eDahab) is used everywhere, even in small shops.
travelGuide.safetyBody: Hargeisa is generally safe for visitors who take normal precautions. Dress modestly, avoid photographing government or military buildings, and check locally for the latest security guidance before travel.
travelGuide.emergencyBody: Police: 999 · Hargeisa Group Hospital: available via hotel front desk · Always keep your hotel's address and phone number with you.
travelGuide.internetBody: Local SIM cards (Telesom, Somtel) are inexpensive and easy to buy with a passport. Data coverage is solid in the city center; most hotels and cafes also offer WiFi.
travelGuide.customsBody: Somaliland is a conservative Muslim society. Dress modestly, greet with your right hand, and expect Friday to be a rest day for many businesses.
travelGuide.bestTimeBody: November to February offers the coolest, most comfortable weather. The rainy season (April–May) can make travel outside the city harder.
travelGuide.packingBody: Light, modest clothing (long sleeves and trousers/long skirts recommended), a scarf for women, comfortable walking shoes, sun protection, and a universal power adapter.
travelGuide.faq1Q: Do I need a visa to visit Hargeisa?
travelGuide.faq1A: Most travelers can get a Somaliland visa on arrival at the airport, though it's worth checking current requirements for your nationality before you fly.
travelGuide.faq2A: Hargeisa is considered one of the more stable and welcoming cities in the region, but as with any destination, it's wise to stay informed and use common-sense precautions.
travelGuide.faq3Q: What language is spoken in Hargeisa?
travelGuide.faq3A: Somali is the primary language, with Arabic and English also widely understood, especially in hotels and among younger residents.

hijamaEducation.title: Hijama & Cupping Therapy, Explained
hijamaEducation.intro: Hijama (cupping) is a traditional wellness practice with deep roots in the Prophetic tradition. This is general information to help you know what to expect — it is not medical advice.

whatIs.title: What is Hijama?
whatIs.body1: Hijama is a form of cupping therapy in which small cups create gentle suction on the skin over specific points of the body. It is one of the oldest known wellness practices and is strongly encouraged in the Sunnah.
whatIs.body2: A typical session takes 30–45 minutes. Many people describe it as relaxing, with a feeling of lightness afterwards.

wetVsDry.title: Wet cupping vs. dry cupping
wetVsDry.body1: In dry cupping, cups are placed on the skin to draw suction only — nothing else. It is often used for muscle tension and relaxation.
wetVsDry.body2: In wet cupping (the classical Hijama), the skin is first cupped, then very small, superficial scratches are made and the cups reapplied to draw a small amount of blood. Single-use, sterile blades and cups should always be used.

commonUses.title: What people commonly use it for
commonUses.body: Hijama is most commonly sought for back, neck and shoulder tension, headaches and migraines, general fatigue, stress and relaxation, and overall wellbeing. Experiences vary from person to person.
commonUses.note: Hijama is a wellness practice, not a substitute for medical care. If you have a health condition, are pregnant, take blood-thinning medication, or have a bleeding disorder, speak to your doctor first.

points.title: Common cupping points
points.body: A practitioner selects points based on your goals and comfort. The nape of the neck and upper back (al-kahil) is the most well-known point and is mentioned in the Sunnah; the shoulders, mid-back and lower back are also frequently used.
points.caption: Common points on the upper body (schematic)

preparation.title: How to prepare
preparation.body: Eat a light meal 2–3 hours before your session and stay hydrated. Avoid heavy exercise, caffeine and smoking beforehand. Wear comfortable, loose clothing, and let the practitioner know about any medication you take or health conditions you have.

aftercare.title: Aftercare
aftercare.body: Rest for the remainder of the day and avoid strenuous activity, hot showers, swimming and sauna for about 24 hours. Keep the cupping area clean and covered, drink plenty of water, and eat light, nourishing food. Any marks fade on their own, usually within a few days to two weeks.

hygiene.title: Hygiene & safety
hygiene.body: Every session should use single-use, sterile blades and cups, fresh gloves, and a clean treatment area, with proper disposal of used materials afterwards. If you are ever unsure, it is completely reasonable to ask your practitioner about their hygiene procedure before you begin.

hijamaEducation.medicalDisclaimer: This information is general and for educational purposes only. It is not medical advice and does not replace consultation with a qualified health professional. Hijama is offered here as wellness support, with no claim to treat, cure or prevent any disease.

sunnah.title: Hijama in the Sunnah
sunnah.intro: Hijama is one of the few remedies specifically encouraged in authentic hadith. A few of the most well-known narrations:
sunnah.text1: “Indeed the best of remedies you have is hijama (cupping).”
sunnah.text2: “If there is any good in the remedies with which you treat yourselves, it is in cupping (hijama).”
sunnah.footnote: Hadith references are provided for the religious virtue of the practice. They are kept separate from, and are not, medical claims.

alHikmaStorefront.heroTagline: A faith-inspired wellness clinic dedicated to health and relaxation through Sunnah Hijama — wet and dry cupping therapy — and massage.

sunnah.title: Rooted in the Sunnah
sunnah.body: Hijama is practised here as a Prophetic tradition, with care and respect.

hygiene.title: Single-use & sterile
hygiene.body: Sterile, single-use cups and blades for every wet cupping session.

specialist.title: Experienced specialist
specialist.body: Sessions are carried out by the clinic's Hijama specialist.

calm.title: Calm, private setting
calm.body: A quiet, comfortable space designed to help you relax.

alHikmaStorefront.overviewImageAlt: A practitioner laying out sterile cups before a Hijama session
alHikmaStorefront.illustrativeNote: Photos are illustrative of Hijama and wellness settings, not the clinic's own premises.

step1.title: Book a time
step1.body: Message or call the clinic to arrange a session that suits you.

step2.title: Come prepared
step2.body: Eat a light meal beforehand, stay hydrated, and wear loose, comfortable clothing.

step3.title: Your session
step3.body: A calm session with the clinic's Hijama specialist — typically 30 to 45 minutes — using sterile, single-use equipment.

alHikmaStorefront.offerFinePrint: For first-time visitors. Confirm availability with the clinic when you book.
alHikmaStorefront.servicesIntro: Choose the session that suits you. The specialist will talk through what to expect before starting.
alHikmaStorefront.servicesDisclaimer: Hijama and massage are traditional wellness practices, not a substitute for medical care. If you are pregnant, take blood-thinning medication, or have a health condition, speak to your doctor first.

hijama.name: Hijama / Cupping Therapy
hijama.body: The classical Hijama session — cups are placed over selected points to draw gentle suction, following the Sunnah.

wet.name: Wet Hijama
wet.body: Cupping followed by very small, superficial scratches so a little blood is drawn, using sterile single-use equipment.

dry.name: Dry Cupping
dry.body: Suction only, with no scratches — often chosen for muscle tension, stiffness, and relaxation.

massage.name: Massage & Wellness
massage.body: A relaxing massage to ease tension in the back, neck, and shoulders, on its own or alongside cupping.
